title: A locally finitely presented birational morphism identifies two dense opens
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] that is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose $X$ and $Y$ have finitely many irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Assume $f$ maps the generic points of the irreducible components of $Y$ bijectively onto those of $X$ [def-sc-generic-point], and for every such generic point $\eta$ of $Y$ the induced homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,f(\eta)}\to\mathcal O_{Y,\eta}$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Then there are dense open subschemes $U\subseteq Y$ and $V\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $f(U)\subseteq V$ and the restriction $f|_U:U\to V$ is an isomorphism. No separatedness or reducedness hypothesis is imposed; the conclusion does not assert that $U=f^{-1}(V)$.

proof.text: Let $\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_r$ be the generic points of the irreducible components $Y_1,\ldots,Y_r$ of $Y$ and $\xi_i=f(\eta_i)$; by hypothesis and uniqueness of generic points these are the generic points of the irreducible components $X_1,\ldots,X_r$ of $X$, with $X_i=\overline{\{\xi_i\}}$, $Y_i=\overline{\{\eta_i\}}$. Put $X_i^\circ=X\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}X_j$ and $Y_i^\circ=Y\setminus\bigcup_{j\ne i}Y_j$: open (finite unions of closed sets), pairwise disjoint, $X_i^\circ\subseteq X_i$, $Y_i^\circ\subseteq Y_i$, and $\xi_i\in X_i^\circ$, $\eta_i\in Y_i^\circ$ (if $\xi_i\in X_j$ then $X_i\subseteq X_j$, so $i=j$ by maximality). By the affine-open basis choose an affine open $V_i^0=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X_i^\circ$ containing $\xi_i$, and then an affine open $U_i^0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y_i^\circ\cap f^{-1}(V_i^0)$ containing $\eta_i$ (this open contains $\eta_i$ since $f(\eta_i)=\xi_i$). By the affine-chart square, under the identifications $U_i^0=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $V_i^0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ the restriction $f|_{U_i^0}:U_i^0\to V_i^0$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for the ring map $\varphi:B\to A$ induced by $f$. A nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is irreducible and dense, so $\operatorname{Spec}B$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ are irreducible with generic points $\xi_i$, $\eta_i$; by the description of the irreducible components of a spectrum, these correspond to the unique minimal primes $\mathfrak q\subset B$ and $\mathfrak p\subset A$. Steps 2--4 are carried out for each $i$ separately with this notation.

source.place: Tag 0BAC, lemma-birational-birational, proof: “There is an immediate reduction to the case where X and Y are irreducible which we omit. Moreover, after shrinking further we may assume X and Y are affine”.

proof.text: The hypothesis on the generic points gives $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak q$. By the stalk-localization description for affine schemes, the map on stalks at the generic points is exactly $B_{\mathfrak q}\to A_{\mathfrak p}$, and it is an isomorphism by assumption. Apply the generic-localization lemma above to obtain an isomorphism $B_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 0BAC, lemma-birational-birational, proof: “By Lemma \ref{lemma-birational-generic-fibres} we have B_q = A_q = A_p”, with the proof of Tag 0BAB (lemma-birational-generic-fibres).

proof.text: The affine morphism is locally of finite presentation, hence its ring map is of finite presentation and in particular has finitely many algebra generators. Choose generators $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of $A$ over $B$. Since $B_{\mathfrak q}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$ is surjective, each $x_i$ is $b_i/g_i$ with $g_i\notin\mathfrak q$. Equality after localization gives another $g_i'\notin\mathfrak q$ with $g_i'(b_i-g_ix_i)=0$. For $g=\prod_i g_ig_i'$, the map $B_g\to A_g$ is surjective. Its kernel is finitely generated: $A_g=A\otimes_BB_g$ is finitely presented over $B_g$ (base change of a presentation $B[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/(h_1,\ldots,h_m)$ of $A$), and the kernel lemma applies to the surjection $B_g\to A_g$ (polynomial ring in $0$ variables); each kernel generator vanishes after localization at $\mathfrak q$, so multiplying $g$ by finitely many further elements outside $\mathfrak q$ makes the kernel zero. Thus, after replacing $g$, $B_g\xrightarrow{\sim}A_g$.

source.place: Tag 0BAC, lemma-birational-birational, proof, finite-presentation case (2), together with Tag 01TQ.

proof.text: For each $i$, put $V_i=D(g)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B=V_i^0$ and $U_i=(\operatorname{Spec}\varphi)^{-1}(V_i)=D(\varphi(g))\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A=U_i^0$. By the principal-localization lemma these are open subschemes identified with $\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A_g$, and $f|_{U_i}:U_i\to V_i$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $B_g\to A_g$, an isomorphism by Step 3. They are nonempty since $\xi_i\in V_i$ ($g\notin\mathfrak q$) and $\eta_i\in U_i$ ($\varphi(g)\notin\mathfrak p$, as $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak p)=\mathfrak q$).

source.place: Tag 0BAC, conclusion of the affine proof.

proof.text: Set $U=\bigcup_iU_i\subseteq Y$ and $V=\bigcup_iV_i\subseteq X$. Since $U_i\subseteq Y_i^\circ$ and $V_i\subseteq X_i^\circ$, these are disjoint unions of open subschemes, $f(U_i)\subseteq V_i$ gives $f(U)\subseteq V$, and $f|_U:U\to V$ is the disjoint union of the isomorphisms $f|_{U_i}:U_i\to V_i$, hence an isomorphism. $U$ contains every $\eta_i$, so $\overline U\supseteq\bigcup_iY_i=Y$; likewise $V$ contains every $\xi_i$, so $\overline V\supseteq\bigcup_iX_i=X$, since every point of $X$ lies in an irreducible component and the $X_i$ are all of them.

source.place: Tag 0BAC, first sentence and final “This proves case (2)” reduction.
